units.translation: Aeschylus called the Bacchae χαλιμάδας [loose women] in fr. 377, about which Hermann says: "It seems to be referred to the Edoni that the schol. Apoll. Rh. 1, 473 cites: Αἰσχύλος δὲ καὶ τὰς Βάκχας χαλιμίας φησὶ λέγεσθαι (χαλίδας ἔφη apogr. Paris.) [Aeschylus says that the Bacchae are also called chalimiai (the Paris apograph has chalidas)]. I correct: Αἰσχύλος δὲ καὶ τὰς Βάκχας χαλιμάδας, φασί, λέγει. Εtym. Μ. p. 805, 10. [Aeschylus, they say, calls the Bacchae chalimadas. Etym. M. p. 805, 10.] καὶ τὰς Βάκχας χαλιμάδας ἔλεγον, τὰς χαλωμένας πρὸς συνουσίαν· καὶ χαλιμάζειν τὸ περὶ τὰς συνουσίας πείθεσθαι [And they called the Bacchae chalimadas, those who are loosened for intercourse; and chalimazein means to be persuaded about intercourse]. Suidas: χαλίμα: ἡ πόρνη, ἀπὸ τοῦ χαλᾶσθαι τὸ σῶμα ἀπὸ μέθης ἢ μανίας [chalima: the prostitute, from the body being loosened from drunkenness or madness]. More correctly written in Eust. p. 1471, 3. εἰ δὲ πρὸς τὰς τοιαύτας διάφοροί τινες ἦσαν αἱ κατ᾽ Αἰσχύλον σπονδαί χαλίκρητοι Ζητητέον· τοιαῦται δὲ αἱ ἐπὶ Διονύσῳ κραθεῖσαι· χάλις γάρ, φασίν, ὁ Διόνυσος· ἐξ ἐκείνου δὲ καὶ ὁ ἄκρατος οἶνος. ὅθεν καὶ χαλιμὰς γυνὴ κατὰ τοὺς παλαιοὺς ἡ ὑπὸ μέθης χα λωμένη τὸ σῶμα [But if the chalikretoi libations in Aeschylus were different from such, it must be investigated; such are those mixed for Dionysus; for chalis, they say, is Dionysus; and from him also the unmixed wine. Hence also a chalimas woman, according to the ancients, is one whose body is loosened by drunkenness]. Hesychius: χαλιμάδες: ἀναίσχυντοι καὶ θρασεῖαι [chalimades: shameless and bold]. I believe χαλειμάδας [loose-robed women], lax garments, were meant. What Eustathius attributes to Aeschylus, σπονδαὶ χαλίκρητοι [unmixed libations], is not Aeschylus's, but Archilochus's, who said χαλίκρητον μέθυ [unmixed wine]: see under σπονδή [libation].
Aeschylus says that the Bacchae are also called chalimiai (the Paris apograph has chalidas)
Aeschylus, they say, calls the Bacchae chalimadas. Etym. M
And they called the Bacchae chalimadas, those who are loosened for intercourse; and chalimazein means to be persuaded about intercourse
chalima: the prostitute, from the body being loosened from drunkenness or madness

But if the chalikretoi libations in Aeschylus were different from such, it must be investigated; such are those mixed for Dionysus; for chalis, they say, is Dionysus; and from him also the unmixed wine. Hence also a chalimas woman, according to the ancients, is one whose body is loosened by drunkenness
